Hello, Spectator!

Welcome to my confessional! I plan to be talking about my POV of the game in here at least once every 2-3 days, and I am known to go on very long rants. The first thing you will probably notice if you scroll up is that I lied about my fun fact! I know many of you will have drafted or not drafted me based on nothing but my cast reveal information, which includes my fun fact, so the first question you might find yourself asking is: why? Good question! My strategy for the game will depend a lot on what Patron I draw, but I plan to make the best use of my ability that I possibly can. I am a defensive, social player, and will likely get a defensive ability to help with this play style. My MO is to set up the social dynamics of the tribe so that killing me is extremely difficult, but doing it sneakily so that it isn't apparent how insulated I am. I am typically pretty good at the pre-merge, since I am able to connect with most people easily and form in majority alliances without becoming too much of a threat, but I have never made the final tribal council before in the two Survivors and various other ORGs I have played, so we will see how that goes. This season, I will be working on my reputation. The thing that has gotten me killed in most if not all past ORGs I have played is that I develop a reputation of being a scary and powerful player that would win at the final tribal council, so this season I will be working to maintain a reputation that is more under-the-radar and less obvious as to what I am doing. That doesn't mean I won't be making plays though! Just picking my battles. Lastly, I will say here that I have a very strong sense of humor and will post about anything particularly funny that happens to my confessional. This includes me lying for fun like you saw, which I plan to do a lot because I think it's funny that I can get away with it. I hope you enjoy watching the season and that I manage to put on a good show for you! :)

Aphrodite A1: Match Made In Heaven Once per game, Aphrodite may change the format. Pre-Merge: Im the realms that are holding a sacrifice, everyone must pick a player to "couple" with - if that person picks them back, they form a couple. If two people form a couple and vote differently, both their votes do not count. Anyone who does not find a couple has incoming votes on them multiplied by 2 during the sacrifice, but can vote normally. Aphrodite may force up to one couple in each realm to form, which is announced to the players in that realm. Merge: Only usable when an odd number of players are alive. Everyone must pick a player to form a "couple" with - if that person picks them back, they are both immune for the round. If only one person remains uncoupled, they are instantly eliminated, otherwise, everyone in a couple votes on someone who isn't, and the player with the most votes is eliminated. In addition, Aphrodite gets to choose what up to half (rounded down) of the possible couples will be, and these are announced to everyone. A2: Twisted Desire Twice per game, Aphrodite may pick another Herald to "charm" for one round. While they are charmed, she gains full control of their abilities and vote; however, she is not told what patron or abilities her target has, and if she tries to use an ability that her target doesn't have, they become un-charmed. Lexi [S2 - 2nd] 2026-05-19 1:23 AM

WHY I TOOK HYDRO TO FTC

I think it is extremely easy to sit back from a spectator perspective and call what I did stupid, a mistake, the wrong play, etc. I obviously should have not taken Hydro, Veejay was never ever winning and even if Wendi was the threat I thought they were I still would have had an easier time going up against just them and not having to deal with Hydro. The thing some of you seem to potentially be missing is the fact that I knew this. Yes, I did have some delusions of grandeur that made me think I stood a real chance against Hydro in FTC when in reality it was not close. Yes, it was a bad play strategically. But I take issue with calling it stupid, or calling it a mistake. That is disrespectful to my agency as a person. Even if I had not thought that I stood a good chance against Hydro, I still would have taken him to F3. My experience in orgs has been one of constantly getting my chance snatched away from me by people who I trust. In my first org, I got betrayed by the other two members of my F3 deal. In my second one, I got ousted by two of my closer allies due to a twist. In my third, I was betrayed by my best friend. In my fourth, I was blindsided by all three of my most trusted allies. In every single one of these cases, one of the people who betrayed me went on to win the game. And they have always been closer to someone else than they were to me. They never trusted me as much as I trusted them. It fucking hurt, and it reminded me of my childhood in a very bad way. So when I came into the merge with less than nothing left after the f14 round, I thought that obviously this would happen again. That I would try to get close to someone, and then they would have someone else who they were more loyal to than me, and cut me out late in the game just when I was beginning to get my hopes up. I was bracing for impact before it even came.
1:23 AM
And then, as much as I may have manipulated him into doing so, Hydro started talking to me, and it became extremely apparent that he was NOT faking his loyalty to me. That he genuinely meant it when he said that he trusted me. That I was his honest-to-god number 1, despite all of his other allies that he had for longer than me. I knew he was not faking it. He proved it to me on F10 by sticking his neck out for me. He went along with basically all of my plans, I was the one who came up with most of the strategic ideas in our VCs. And even if it wasn't true, he GENUINELY BELIEVED that he would lose to me on Final Tribal, and as much as I may have manipulated him into doing so, he was willing to take me there ANYWAY. So when we had gotten down to F6, finished making all the moves that I had guided us through for my own benefit, and it became apparent that I would be making final tribal pretty much no matter what, I had already proven everything I needed to prove to myself. I was capable of not being the one who was left out. But I was still faced with the choice. Do I take the easy and (more or less) guaranteed win of me/silent/veejay at FTC, and exclude Hydro from what I understand to have been his first real chance at winning an org, like had been done to me so many times before? Or do I accept the possibility that I could lose to Hydro, and take him to FTC anyway? To me, the choice was obvious. (edited)
1:23 AM
I will conclude by reiterating what I said earlier. I think it is extremely easy to sit back from a spectator perspective and call what I did stupid, a mistake, the wrong play, etc. But quite frankly, none of you were there in those calls that I had with Hydro, late at night, strategizing, laughing, and struggling together. None of you felt the same things I did, having been given a second chance at life in the game by this man who was so unspeakably genuine, so kind, and so obviously ready to defend me with his life. And none of you seem to think this could possibly have been anything more than a meaningless game to me. What I did was not stupid, nor was it a mistake. I knew it was a bad strategic decision, and I made it anyway. I am sorry to all the people who I disappointed who wanted me to win, but I am extremely fucking proud of myself for this result, and for my own sake, I will not be letting anyone convince me of why I shouldn't be. Congrats on your win, Hydro. - Lexi (edited)
